item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one table in a pair of adjacent tables. This is one endpoint of an adjacency relation; identifiers are table numbers between 1 and total_tables.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other table in the adjacent pair. Together with adjacent_table_1, it denotes two tables that are next to each other and cannot both be selected to be dressed.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of books placed on the shelf — each book is a vertex you could consider for the front display. This is the count of distinct books available.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of pairs of books that are directly next to each other on the shelf. Each such pair represents an adjacency (an edge) and means you may not choose both books in that pair for the display.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one book in an adjacent pair (an endpoint of an edge). Together with 'v' it names two books that sit next to each other on the shelf and therefore cannot both be selected for the front display.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other book in an adjacent pair (the other endpoint of an edge). Paired with 'u' this marks a neighboring-book relationship that forbids choosing both books for the display.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct channel knobs on the wall — i.e., the number of available broadcast channels you can choose to turn on or leave off.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of interfering pairs of channels — each pair represents two knobs that cannot both be switched to "on" because they clash.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of one channel in a specific interference pair — one of the two knobs that conflict for this listed pair.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of the other channel in the same interference pair — the second knob that cannot be turned on at the same time as channel_one.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of wall panels (equivalently the total number of paintings/positions) in the exhibition layout. This is the count of all vertices in the panel-adjacency map.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency relationships between panels. Each counts a pair of panels that are next to each other (an edge) and therefore cannot both hold selected paintings.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of one panel in an adjacent pair. Used together with 'v' to describe two panels that share a border and thus cannot both have paintings displayed.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of the other panel in an adjacent pair. Together with 'u' it defines a pair of neighboring panels that cannot both be chosen for displaying paintings.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of households on the street (the number of vertices). Each household is a candidate to invite and must be considered exactly once when building the guest list.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairs of neighboring households (the number of undirected edges). Each pair represents two next-door homes that cannot both be invited to the block celebration.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or address label) of one household in a neighboring pair. This denotes one endpoint of an adjacency relation: household_a is next-door to household_b and both must not be invited together.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or address label) of the other household in the same neighboring pair. This denotes the other endpoint of an adjacency relation: household_b is next-door to household_a and both must not be invited together.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of students in the classroom seating chart (the number of vertices). This is the count of distinct students you can potentially choose for solo presentations.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairs of students who are seated next to each other (the number of undirected adjacency relationships). Each such pair represents a prohibition: you may not select both students in that pair for solo presentations.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (for example, seat number or student label) of one student in a specific adjacent pair. Together with 'student_v_id' this denotes two students who are seated next to each other and therefore cannot both be chosen.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (seat number or student label) of the other student in the same adjacent pair. The pair (student_u_id, student_v_id) describes an undirected adjacency — selecting one forbids selecting the other.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of servers in the rack/network. This is the count of distinct machines (vertices) you can choose from when powering servers for active duty.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of direct connections (undirected cables) between servers. Each cable links two servers that cannot both be powered simultaneously.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a cable: the identifier for the first server involved in a direct connection. If this server is powered, the paired server (v) must remain off.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a cable: the identifier for the second server involved in a direct connection. This and the server in 'server_endpoint_u' cannot both be powered at the same time.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of hangers (each holding one unique garment) available in the boutique; this is the count of possible display positions (vertices) you can choose from for the window.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of neighboring-hanger pairs; each pair represents two hangers that are physically adjacent on the rack and therefore cannot both be used to display garments at the same time.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for one hanger in an adjacency pair — a specific hanger index or label. Combined with 'hanger_b', it denotes a pair of neighboring hangers that cannot both be chosen for the window.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for the other hanger in the adjacency pair — paired with 'hanger_a' to specify two adjacent hangers that are mutually exclusive for display.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of benches along the promenade — the count of distinct bench locations that can be considered for refurbishment (bench identifiers run from 1 to this number).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency relationships between benches — each represents a pair of benches that sit next to each other along the promenade and therefore cannot both be selected for refurbishment.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One bench in an adjacency pair: the identifier for the first bench of two benches that are directly adjacent along the promenade (if both are chosen, that would violate the no-adjacent rule).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other bench in an adjacency pair: the identifier for the second bench directly adjacent to bench_a along the promenade.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of plants (positions) in the border that you, the gardener, are considering; this is the count of vertices from which you may choose plants to keep or remove.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of adjacency relationships between plants in the border; each represents a pair of neighboring plants whose roots would touch, meaning the two in that pair cannot both be kept.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the first plant in a specific adjacent pair; refers to one endpoint of an edge (one plant position) in the layout.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the second plant in the same adjacent pair; together with 'plant_one_id' it marks two neighboring plants whose roots would interfere if both were kept.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of available parade-route spots (vertices). This is the number of distinct positions where a single performer can be scheduled; identifiers for spots will be in the range provided by the instance.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency relations (edges) between spots. Each adjacency indicates a pair of neighboring spots on the route that cannot both be occupied by performers at the same time.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the first spot in an adjacent pair. Together with 'v' this denotes two neighboring spots on the parade route that conflict (you cannot schedule performers in both).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the second spot in an adjacent pair. Paired with 'u', it marks the other spot that is adjacent and therefore cannot be filled simultaneously with 'u'.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of tables in the dining area (each table is a vertex that can be either reserved for the private event or left available).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of side-by-side table adjacencies (each adjacency is an edge representing a pair of tables that cannot both be reserved).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one table in a specific side-by-side pair; paired with 'adjacent_table_2' to indicate two neighboring tables that cannot both be reserved.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other table in the same side-by-side pair; paired with 'adjacent_table_1' to indicate two neighboring tables that cannot both be reserved.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of compartments in the traveling case; each compartment holds one artifact and corresponds to a vertex in the graph. This is the count of candidate artifacts the registrar may choose from.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency relationships between compartments (undirected edges). Each listed pair means those two compartments are directly next to each other, so if an artifact is taken from one, the artifact in the adjacent compartment cannot be taken.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an adjacency relationship: the identifier of a compartment containing an artifact. Together with 'compartment_v' it denotes a pair of directly adjacent compartments that cannot both be selected.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of an adjacency relationship: the identifier of a compartment directly next to 'compartment_u'. The pair (compartment_u, compartment_v) indicates two compartments whose artifacts are mutually exclusive for selection.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of microphone channels available in the venue diagram (each channel is a single vertex). Use this to know how many distinct channels can potentially be activated.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of direct crosstalk relationships between channels (each is an edge). Each counted pair represents two channels that must not be turned on together.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of the first microphone channel in a direct-crosstalk pair. Together with 'mic_channel_v' this specifies two channels that cannot both be active.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of the second microphone channel in a direct-crosstalk pair. Paired with 'mic_channel_u' to indicate an interfering (forbidden simultaneous) activation.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of bike rack slots available (the number of vertices). This tells you how many distinct slot identifiers exist that the manager can consider approving.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency conflicts between slots (the number of edges). Each count here corresponds to an unordered pair of neighboring slots that cannot both be approved at the same time.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or label) of one rack slot in a conflicting pair. This is one endpoint of an adjacency relationship: if this slot is approved, the paired slot must not be.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or label) of the other rack slot in the conflicting pair. Together with 'slot_u' it defines two adjacent slots that cannot both be allowed.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of campsites in the park layout. This is the count of distinct campsite locations that the ranger must decide to keep open or close.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency relationships between campsites. Each represents a pair of campsites that are next to each other and therefore cannot both be kept open.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the first campsite in an adjacent pair. Paired with 'campsite_b', it marks two neighboring sites where the ranger cannot leave both open.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the second campsite in an adjacent pair. Together with 'campsite_a' it denotes a direct adjacency (an edge) forbidding both sites from being kept open.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct crates (vertices) in the aisle that the clerk can consider moving to the front.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of neighboring-pallet relationships: each counts a pair of crates that sit on adjacent pallets and therefore cannot both be moved.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one crate in a neighboring pair. Together with 'v' it denotes two crates on adjacent pallets that cannot both be chosen.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other crate in the neighboring pair. The pair (u, v) marks two crates on adjacent pallets that cannot both be moved.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of booths in the hall layout. Interpreted as the number of vertices in the graph; every booth is a unique vertex that can potentially be marked for priority lighting.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency relationships between booths. Interpreted as the number of edges in the graph; each edge represents a pair of neighboring booths that cannot both be selected for priority lighting.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an undirected adjacency pair: the identifier for the first booth in a neighboring-booth relationship. Used together with 'v' to indicate two booths that are adjacent and therefore cannot both receive priority lighting.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of an undirected adjacency pair: the identifier for the second booth in a neighboring-booth relationship. Paired with 'u' to denote a specific edge (neighboring pair) in the hall layout.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of lineup positions along the parade route that could be staffed (labels like 1..N). This is the maximum pool of spots you can choose helpers from.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency relationships between positions. Each adjacency (edge) marks a pair of neighboring lineup spots that cannot both be staffed at the same time.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an adjacent pair: the identifier of the first lineup position in a neighboring pair (a spot index). If this position is staffed, its paired position must not be staffed.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of an adjacent pair: the identifier of the second lineup position in the neighboring pair. Together with position_u, this defines two side-by-side spots that cannot both receive helpers.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of cell sites (base stations) in tonight's network. Every one of these stations requires a definitive on/off decision; the goal is to maximize how many of these are switched on without violating interference constraints.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of directly interfering pairs of base stations. Each interference link connects two stations that cannot both be active simultaneously, so each listed link imposes the constraint that at most one endpoint of that link may be live.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of one base station in a directly interfering pair. For the corresponding link line, this is one endpoint of the pair; when choosing active stations, ensure that if this station is on, the paired station (v) must be off.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of the other base station in the same interfering pair. For the corresponding link line, this is the second endpoint of the pair; together with 'station_endpoint_a' it defines a constraint that at most one of the two may be active.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of students under consideration for the assembly presenters (the number of vertices). This tells you how many distinct students are available to choose from.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of pairwise scheduling conflicts between students (the number of edges). Each conflict is a pair of students who have overlapping schedules and therefore cannot both be picked as presenters.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or ID) of one student involved in a specific scheduling conflict. Interpreted together with 'v' to mean these two students have a time clash and only one of them may be chosen.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or ID) of the other student involved in the same scheduling conflict. Paired with 'u' to indicate a mutually exclusive pair for presenter selection.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct dishes available to choose from for the tasting menu (each graph vertex corresponds to one dish).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of unordered dish pairs that clash in ingredients (each graph edge represents a pair of dishes that cannot both be included on the same menu).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one dish in a clashing pair; together with 'dish_b' it denotes two dishes that cannot both be offered on the tasting menu. Identifiers match the vertex numbering of the dishes list.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other dish in a clashing pair; together with 'dish_a' it denotes two dishes that cannot both be offered on the tasting menu. The pair is unordered (clash is mutual).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of people who offered to help at the block fair (each is a vertex). Use this to know how many distinct volunteer identifiers exist to choose from.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of known personal conflicts between volunteers (each is an undirected edge). This counts how many pairs of people cannot both be signed up.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a conflict pair: the identifier (index or name) of the first volunteer in a known personal conflict. If this person is chosen, the paired volunteer cannot be chosen.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the same conflict pair: the identifier (index or name) of the second volunteer who clashes with volunteer_a. The conflict is mutual, so both cannot be on the roster together.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct candidate tracks the host may choose from when building the one-hour playlist. This is the count of vertices in the conflict graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of station-policy conflict pairs between tracks. Each such pair represents two songs that must not both appear in the same hour-long playlist.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a conflict pair: the identifier (index, title ID, or unique label) for the first track in a policy-incompatible pair. If this track is included, the paired track (v) cannot be included.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a conflict pair: the identifier for the second track in a policy-incompatible pair. This track cannot be scheduled together with the corresponding track (u) in the same hour-long playlist.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct songs being considered for the live set (each song is a single vertex). This is the size of the pool from which you may select the lineup.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of unordered song pairs that are incompatible (an edge between two songs means they cannot follow one another and therefore cannot both be chosen).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one song in a specific incompatible pair. Together with song_b_id it marks a pair of songs that cannot both appear in the chosen set.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other song in this incompatible pair. This and song_a_id define an edge: the two named songs cannot both be in the live lineup.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of desks on the floorplan — i.e., the number of people/positions available (graph vertices).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of conflict pairs: how many pairs of desks are marked as "shouldn't sit together" (graph edges).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first desk in a conflict pair — one endpoint of a "shouldn't sit together" relationship.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second desk in a conflict pair — the other endpoint of a "shouldn't sit together" relationship.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct activities available to choose from for the weekend roster; each activity corresponds to a vertex in the conflict graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairwise conflicts between activities; each conflict represents a pair of activities that cannot both be scheduled.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (name or index) of one activity in a conflicting pair; used with 'activity_b' to indicate these two activities clash and cannot both be included.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (name or index) of the other activity in the conflicting pair; together with 'activity_a' it defines a conflict edge between the two activities.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct readings available to choose from for the ceremony.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairwise clashes between readings (each clash means those two readings cannot both be included).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One of the two readings involved in a clash pair; this identifier refers to a specific reading option.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other reading in the clash pair; together with reading_a, it denotes a pair that cannot both be selected for the ceremony.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of individual animals listed as candidates for the communal playroom. This is the number of vertices in the conflict graph and tells you how many distinct animals may be approved.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairs of animals that fight and therefore cannot be released together. This is the number of undirected edges in the graph and sets how many conflict constraints there are to respect when approving animals.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for one animal in a fighting pair. Together with the corresponding 'animal_b_id' on the same line, it denotes two animals that must not both be approved for the same playroom session.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for the other animal in a fighting pair. Paired with 'animal_a_id', it marks an undirected conflict: the two named animals cannot both be chosen for the communal play area.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of distinct shrub varieties available to consider for the bed; each variety corresponds to a vertex in the graph of chemical interactions.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of harmful pairwise relationships between shrub varieties; each edge represents two varieties that release chemicals that hurt each other and therefore cannot both be planted side by side.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or label) of one shrub variety in a specific conflict pair. Together with 'v' this marks two varieties that must not both be planted in the bed.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or label) of the other shrub variety in the same conflict pair. This and 'u' define a harmful interaction preventing both varieties from being chosen together.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct accessory items available to place on the window mannequin. This is the number of vertices in the conflict graph and equals the maximum possible count you could select if there were no clashes.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairwise stylistic clashes between accessories. Each clash is an edge in the graph and represents a pair of items that cannot both be included in the display.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the first accessory in a conflicting pair. Used together with 'accessory_b' to denote a clash: these two uniquely labeled items must not both be chosen for the display.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the second accessory in a conflicting pair. Paired with 'accessory_a' to indicate a stylistic clash (an edge): do not select both items simultaneously.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct speakers on the conference roster (each graph vertex). This is the pool of people you may invite; the maximum possible panel size before excluding conflicting pairs.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of unordered pairs of speakers who have a public disagreement (each graph edge). Each conflict prohibits inviting both members of that pair to the panel.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one speaker in a conflicting pair (one endpoint of an edge). This references a specific person from the roster; if both this speaker and the paired speaker are invited, that violates the no-disagreement rule.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other speaker in the conflicting pair (the other endpoint of an edge). Together with speaker_id_a it denotes two people who have publicly argued and therefore cannot both be invited.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct short films on the roster that could be programmed into the single festival block. This corresponds to the number of vertices in the conflict graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of unordered licensing conflicts between pairs of films. Each conflict is an edge indicating the two named films cannot both be scheduled in the block.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one film in a conflicting pair (e.g., an index or title ID). Used together with 'v' to denote an undirected licensing conflict between two films.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other film in the conflicting pair. Paired with 'u' to indicate the two films cannot both be included in the programmed block.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of neighborhood members being considered for patrol shifts — the full candidate pool; count each person once.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of refusing-pair relationships (pairs of people who won’t work together). Each edge represents one mutually incompatible pair that cannot both be chosen.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One member of a refusing pair (given by the same identifier or name used in the member list). Together with 'person_b' this denotes two people who cannot both be on the patrol team.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other member of the refusing pair (identifier or name). The order with 'person_a' does not matter — the refusal is mutual and both cannot be selected together.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct recipes considered for the themed chapter (the number of vertices). Use this to understand the range of recipe identifiers and the size of the selection pool.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of unordered pairs of recipes that either duplicate or contradict each other (the number of edges). Each such pair cannot both be included in the final chapter.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One recipe identifier in a conflicting/duplicate pair. Together with 'recipe_b_id' this item describes a pair of recipes that must not both be chosen.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other recipe identifier in a conflicting/duplicate pair. Pairs (recipe_a_id, recipe_b_id) are symmetric: they mark two recipes that conflict (an edge between their vertices).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct vendor booths under consideration for the single row — i.e., the total number of vendors (vertices) you may choose from.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of incompatible vendor pairs — each counts an observed refusal between two vendors who must not both be accepted into the row (each edge represents such a conflict).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for one vendor in an incompatible pair. Together with 'v' this names two vendors who refuse to share the event; the order is not significant.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for the other vendor in an incompatible pair. Paired with 'u', it marks a conflict: these two vendors cannot both be accepted into the row.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of feature ideas under consideration for the next release — each feature is a vertex in the conflict graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of known pairwise conflicts between features — each conflict is an edge indicating two features that cannot both be selected.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or name) of the first feature in a conflicting pair; one endpoint of an edge representing a conflict between two features.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or name) of the second feature in a conflicting pair; the other endpoint of an edge representing a conflict between two features.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct performers (bands and soloists) on the venue's roster. In graph terms this is the number of vertices you may choose from when assembling the lineup.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of known pairwise personal or contractual conflicts among performers. Each conflict is an edge indicating two performers that cannot both be invited.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One performer identifier (name or unique ID) forming one end of a known conflict pair. Together with performer_b this defines a pair that cannot both be included in the lineup. The edge is unordered (performer_a vs performer_b is the same as performer_b vs performer_a).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other performer identifier (name or unique ID) forming the second end of a known conflict pair. Paired with performer_a, this denotes a single personal or contractual beef preventing both from being invited simultaneously.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of distinct original framed pictures the homeowner has available to hang — each graph vertex corresponds to one picture.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of known stylistic clash pairs among the pictures; each represents a pair of pictures that cannot be displayed together (an undirected conflict).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of the first picture in a specific clashing pair — one endpoint of a conflict edge; refers to an original framed picture.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of the second picture in the same clashing pair — the other endpoint of the conflict edge; this picture cannot be hung together with the one named by picture_one_id.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct plant species listed as options for the mixed bed. Use this to know how many species identifiers exist and to verify the full species list size.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of known incompatible species pairs. Each count represents a pair of species that are known to compete or inhibit one another and therefore cannot both be chosen for the bed.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the first plant species in a documented incompatible pair. Matches one species from the available list; if chosen, this species cannot be planted together with the species identified by 'species_b_id'.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the second plant species in a documented incompatible pair. Matches one species from the available list; this species cannot be planted together with the species identified by 'species_a_id'.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct artifacts the curator is considering for the single exhibit. This equals the number of vertices in the conflict graph and is the maximum possible headcount before excluding conflicting items.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of provenance or ownership conflict relationships among artifacts. Each counts a pair of items that cannot be shown together (the number of edges in the graph).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for one artifact in a specific conflicting pair. Paired with 'v' (artifact_b), this indicates the two named artifacts have a provenance/ownership issue and therefore cannot both be included in the same exhibit.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for the other artifact in a specific conflicting pair. Together with 'u' (artifact_a), it marks a pair that cannot both appear in the selected exhibit due to provenance/ownership restrictions.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct books the librarian can choose from to place on the promotional table.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of unordered pairs of titles that are restricted from being displayed together (each such pair represents a conflict the curator must avoid).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the first book in a specific restricted pair; paired with 'v' to indicate these two titles cannot appear together on the table.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the second book in a specific restricted pair; together with 'u' defines a disallowed combination of titles for the display.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of available plugins on the site (i.e., the number of vertices). Use this to understand how many distinct plugin identifiers exist and to measure the size of any enabled set.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of known conflict pairs between plugins (i.e., the number of edges). Each conflict prevents the two involved plugins from being enabled together.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one plugin in a conflicting pair. This refers to a plugin from the provided plugin list; together with 'plugin_b' it denotes a conflict edge meaning these two cannot both be enabled.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other plugin in the conflicting pair. Order does not matter: the pair (plugin_a, plugin_b) represents an undirected conflict between those two plugins.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of article submissions being considered for the special issue. Each submission corresponds to a vertex in the graph (a candidate the editor may accept).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairwise overlap flags (conflicts) among submissions. Each flag corresponds to an edge indicating two articles that have been marked as overlapping and therefore cannot both be accepted.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or submission ID) of one article in a flagged overlapping pair. Together with 'v', this denotes a pair of submissions that cannot both be included in the issue.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or submission ID) of the other article in a flagged overlapping pair. Together with 'u', this denotes a pair of submissions that cannot both be included in the issue.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct light sets the homeowner has available to hang — i.e., the number of vertices in the incompatibility graph. Identifiers for sets run from 1..this value (or follow whatever labeling the instance uses).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of unordered incompatible pairs of light sets — i.e., the number of edges. Each entry represents two sets that cannot be turned on together and therefore cannot both be chosen in the display.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of one light set in an incompatible pair. This is one endpoint of an incompatibility edge; do not select this set together with the set named by 'v'.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of the other light set in the incompatible pair. Together with 'u' it forms an undirected incompatibility edge — selecting both is forbidden.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct filmmakers being considered for invitations. Each filmmaker corresponds to a vertex in the conflict graph (typically indexed 1..N or 0..N-1 in the instance).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct pairs of filmmakers who have public disputes. Each such pair is an edge in the graph and indicates the two filmmakers cannot both be invited.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index) of the first filmmaker in a disputed pair. Together with 'v' this marks a conflict between two filmmakers who must not both appear on the invited roster.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index) of the second filmmaker in a disputed pair. The pair (u, v) represents an undirected conflict — order is irrelevant and both cannot be invited together.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct volunteers in the neighborhood pool. This tells the organizer how many people are available (each volunteer is assigned a unique identifier from the set used in the roster).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of documented conflict pairs between volunteers. Each conflict pair represents two people who have prior disagreements and therefore cannot both be recruited onto the same team.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One volunteer in a conflicting pair, given by their identifier. Together with 'volunteer_b' this entry marks a pair that must not both appear on the final roster.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other volunteer in a conflicting pair, given by their identifier. The pair (volunteer_a, volunteer_b) indicates a prior conflict preventing both from being recruited simultaneously.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct startups on the investor's shortlist — i.e., the number of vertices in the exclusivity graph (each startup may be chosen at most once).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of exclusivity pacts between startups on the shortlist — i.e., the number of undirected edges in the graph, each forbidding funding both endpoints together.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or label) of one startup in an exclusivity pair; combined with 'v', this item denotes two startups that cannot both be funded.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or label) of the other startup in the exclusivity pair; with 'u' it marks a forbidden pair for simultaneous funding.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct tree varieties available for planting (each graph vertex corresponds to one variety). Use this to understand how many unique variety identifiers exist.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of known cross-inhibiting pairs among the available varieties (each graph edge represents a pair of varieties that cannot both be selected).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a cross-inhibiting pair: the identifier for the first tree variety in a forbidden pair (corresponds to a vertex identifier from the available list).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a cross-inhibiting pair: the identifier for the second tree variety in a forbidden pair (corresponds to a vertex identifier from the available list).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct mantel decorations available to choose from — the count of vertices, i.e., how many individual ornaments exist to potentially place on the mantel.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of known bad pairs of decorations — the count of edges, each representing a pair of ornaments that topple or interfere and therefore cannot both be selected.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One member of a conflicting pair: the identifier (index or name) of the first ornament in this bad pair. Identifiers refer to the list of available decorations.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other member of the conflicting pair: the identifier (index or name) of the second ornament in this bad pair. The pair (ornament_one, ornament_two) is unordered — both cannot be placed together.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate live acts considered for the reception. Each act corresponds to one vertex in the graph and this count tells the planner how many distinct performers are in the pool.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairwise incompatibilities between acts. Each edge represents a conflict (personal dislike, scheduling overlap, etc.) that prevents the two linked acts from both being booked.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One performer identifier in a conflict pair. Together with the field 'v' it names an unordered pair of acts that cannot both be scheduled for the same reception.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other performer identifier in the same conflict pair. The pair (u, v) denotes two acts that are incompatible and therefore cannot both be on the booked roster.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct student projects available to place in the corridor — i.e., the number of vertices in the graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairwise shared-resource conflicts between projects (each conflict is a pair that cannot be displayed together) — i.e., the number of edges in the graph.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of the first project in a conflicting pair — one endpoint of a conflict edge; this project cannot be exhibited together with the paired project.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of the second project in a conflicting pair — the other endpoint of a conflict edge; this project cannot be exhibited together with the paired project.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct fish species under consideration for the aquarium — i.e., how many different species the hobbyist could potentially choose from.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of known aggressive (incompatible) pairs among the species — each such pair means those two species should not be kept together in the tank.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or numeric ID) for one species in a known-aggressive pair; together with species_b_id this denotes a pair that cannot both be placed in the tank.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or numeric ID) for the other species in a known-aggressive pair; combined with species_a_id this marks an incompatible pair (undirected).
